description:
USER REQUIREMENT (2026-10-24, A): the PPI-bug collection must be EASY TO ADD TO AND REMOVE FROM -> build it as the REGISTRY of docs/parser-review-s525.md Â§7 (one row per bug, id = catalogue Â§, kind token|structure|source|lexer-dies, when/fix/repro/tokens/ppi.fixed_in; consumers = the 1a engine, the canary test with the STALE DETECTOR, the upstream report, the catalogue; the skip-registry pattern).  The c1 checker session designs the row schema against the real 38 and files the kind split.  The ENDGAME it serves is review Â§8.

RULED (USER, 2026-10-24): Option 3 (perl compiles, PCL translates the optree) is OFF -- an exact perl version at transpile time or one parser per perl version is unrealistic, and the compiled-code cache would freeze the compile-time environment (perl folds on it; review Â§4 Option 3 risk 2).  The spike below is CANCELLED; this task now carries Option 1 in the revised order.  Cadence: ONE of the two slots per round (the perf slot shape), the other slot keeps the correctness / board batches.  NOT pushed to later: Parser2 grows +12k lines / 90 days, every corner case landed in the old shape is migration surface.

STEP 0 -- TWO INERT CHECKERS (one session each, zero emission change, corpus-diff IDENTICAL by construction):
  c1 expect-state checker: walk PPI significant tokens left to right carrying toke.c expect (XSTATE / XTERM / XOPERATOR / XBLOCK / XREF); for every token whose PPI class contradicts the state, LOG (file, line, token, PPI class, expected class) over the four populations; compare the log against the ~35 repair passes: which repairs it predicts, which tokens it flags that no repair touches (new PPI bugs or checker errors -- probe vs perl), which repairs it does NOT predict (a second state needed?).  Deliverable: the table + the PPI-class x expect-state -> correct-class table read off toke.c yyl_* handlers (yyl_slash, yyl_leftcurly, yyl_lt, yyl_percent, yyl_ampersand, yyl_star, yyl_hyphen, yyl_question).
  c2 binder dual-run (s379 Direction A step 1, pad.c rule: visible from the statement AFTER the declaration, OUTER = capture): one early walk assigning every my/our/state/signature param a binding id and resolving every use (code + interpolated via InterpScan) to it; at every call of _binding_at / _ref_shadowed / _block_captures_name assert agreement, DIE with both verdicts on disagreement (PCL_BINDER_CHECK=1); run over corpus + Pl/t + board.  Every disagreement = a live bug or a design error -- probe vs perl, file.

STEP 1 -- 1a ONE expect-state repair pass replacing the ~35 repair passes and all 18 re-serialize-and-reparse sites: re-lex a contradicting span with PPI::Tokenizer (the fragment_doc pattern), re-tag, continue; `{` in XSTATE/XBLOCK takes yyl_leftcurly lookahead (word/string then , or => = anon hash).  Bar: the 38 canary rows (misc-fixes-02.t + ppi-bug-report.t) hold; corpus-diff IDENTICAL; passes 69 -> fewer; re-parse sites 18 -> 0.  2-3 sessions.

STEP 2 -- 1c the binder PORTS, newest consumer first (requalifier -> capture gate + promoter -> span -> state/cond/shadow/emb), each deleting its private resolver; the SWEEP is the gate (name-resolution change, #296 rule); then name-choice moves to emission.  Bar: scope-walk implementations 18 -> 1; Calc.pm transpile 3.7 s -> < 1.5 s; corpus-diff IDENTICAL per port.  5-7 sessions.

STEP 3 -- 1b ONE keyword-class table (prototype("CORE::name") + ~30 syntax keywords) + ONE extent rule per class (FUNC parens; UNIOP one term to the comparison level; LSTOP to the next same-level or/and/xor or ); FUN0 nothing; a user sub takes its prototype class).  Bar: handle_subcalls 1,811 -> < 600; corpus-diff IDENTICAL.  2-3 sessions.

FILLERS: rename Pl/Parser.pm live halves (PrePass / Facts); close the four-kind text seam (use/require, loop-modifier statements, BEGIN, use constant).

STANDING RULE (effective now, s379 Â§8 restated): no new scope walk, no new rename suffix family; once c1 exists, no new repair pass -- a PPI mis-lex becomes a row in its table; until then a new PPI bug gets catalogue section + report row + canary in the SAME commit (principle 13; the report lags the catalogue by Â§5 and Â§32-Â§38 today).

RESIDUES: r1 three stale ppi-upstream-bugs.md Â§ citations (_restore_signature_gid Â§24->Â§32, _brace_glob_slot_symbol Â§24->Â§27, _repair_term_initial_complement Â§20->Â§21); r2 Config -11/-12 identical codes; r3 Parser.pm naming + text seam; r4 nine PPI documents per transpile (the binder is the fix, not a cache).

CANCELLED (kept for the record): the Option 3 spike S1-S5 (op census, version delta, compile-time input census, 40-op slice, eval seam).  Measured before the ruling: ops 396 (5.26.3) -> 400 (5.32.1) -> 422 (5.40.3), none removed; core B::Deparse supports only its own perl; perl folds `use constant D => $ENV{D}; print "x" if D` to an unconditional or absent print, $^P NOOPT does not prevent it.

=== c1 DONE (s525p, 2026-10-24) ===
Shipped (emission-neutral; corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 files): Pl/PPIExpect.pm (the expect-state checker: 39 transition rows, 58 contradiction rows, 264-word keyword table, each row citing toke.c) + tools/ppi-expect-check.pl; Pl/PPIBugs.pm (the registry, 38 rows, review s7 schema: id kind dump title ppi{confirmed,fixed_in} when fix{kind,handler} repro perl tokens{got,want} unblocks tasks); Pl/t/ppi-bugs-registry-01.t (the canary, 76 rows, 0.16 s; stale message "PPI <version> fixed s<id>: set fixed_in", inverse-checked); tools/t/ppi-expect-check.t (12 rows, not in the gate); docs/expect-state-checker-s525.md (D3 measurement + D5 handler sketch).
NUMBERS: four populations, 1,139 files, 891,112 tokens, 1,180 primary rows = 640 in 23 catalogued sections + 540 in 16 NEW shapes (#3740-#3755). The checker PREDICTS 34 of 38; s3 correctly clean (fixed); NOT predicted by construction s13 (source), s27 (accessor), s30 (heredoc content). Kind split: token 28 / structure 7 / source 1 / lexer-dies 2. The canary subsumes 21 of misc-fixes-02.t's 22 CANARY rows (all but the s38 &$cb twin) + its s3 guard (none deleted; 1a deletes them with the repairs).
BARS: gate PASS 332 / 11,362; everyday 116 of 122 BEFORE -> AFTER; docs/ppi-bug-report.t 77 not ok / 14 ok unchanged.
NEXT: c2 (the binder in dual-run), then 1a consumes the tables + the registry (D5 in the doc maps each row to the repair it replaces). Finding: the catalogue s38 prose repro does not reproduce on 1.291 (the report row does).
=== c2 DONE (s525q, 2026-10-24, resumed s526) ===
Shipped (inert; emission identical, no generation bump): Pl/Binder.pm (the binding table, perl pad model, each rule cited to pad.c/op.c/perly.y/toke.c; die|log|TRACE|INJECT modes), 31 hook lines in Pl/Parser2.pm (_binding_at/_ref_shadowed/_block_captures_name wrap their unchanged *_0 bodies; build point after _classify_nested_gotos = document pass 36 of 40), tools/binder-check.pl (+ tools/lib/PCLPopulations.pm, shared with ppi-expect-check.pl), Pl/t/binder-01.t (17 rows, inverse-verified), docs/binder-dual-run-s525.md (rules, measurement, verdicts, cost, D4 port plan).
NUMBERS: refs everyday 2,430 / perl-tests 23,708 / cpan 27,959 / perl t/ 65,764; D sites 0 / 7 / 2 / 13; sweep log mode 2,681 builds, same 6 sites; gate log mode 7,208 builds, 9 rows. Rebuilds after re-parse: 0.
VERDICTS: LEGACY BUG #3800 #3801 #3804 (silent wrong), #3806 (loud refusal; Pl/t/sig-param-shadow-01.t asserts it), #3802 #3803 (benign); BINDER ERROR 3 fixed (\$b[0], bare $ placeholder, $#+/$#- = Token::Magic -> #3805 for the PPI filler); DESIGN GAP: names only in a string-eval text (5 suite sites + 6 gate rows) -> 1c needs a "CV has a string eval" fact.
COST: the table 2-3 % of a transpile (Calc.pm 152 of 5,769 ms, pack.t 114 of 4,880, everyday 0.6 %); with the hooks Calc.pm +6.0 % wall.

BARS: gate PASS 335 / 11,454 unset (rebased) and PASS in log mode; sweep GATE clean TOTAL 18,759 unset and log; corpus-diff IDENTICAL unset + log; everyday 116 = 116.
NEXT: 1a (the expect-state repair pass); 1c's first port = the requalifier (closes #3800 #3801 #3804 by construction); before porting the rename passes, a second dual-run hook on _rename_decl_within.

=== STEP 1d ADOPTED (Fable, s526, 2026-10-24, from docs/codegen-review-s526.md Â§12) ===
The code-generation review found the compiler's structural debt entirely in Parser2's STATEMENT lowering and recommended no separate program: its options C1-C3 join THIS program as step 1d.
  C1 -- the statement CLASSIFIER (target-architecture Â§2.2): ONE `Stmt::classify($ppi_stmt, $env)` returning kind + pre-split spans; `_lower_block_1` / `_lower_stmt` / `_lower_compound` switch on kind and never index token arrays; the s525p expect-state tables (Pl/PPIExpect.pm) are its data.  IDENTICAL emission.  Bar: `_lower_block_1` 1,188 -> under 300 lines; `isa`/`content` shape tests outside the classifier 52 -> 0; corpus-diff IDENTICAL; gate + the sweep.  2-3 sessions.  Runs right after 1a (the classifier is what makes 1a's tables consumable).
  C2 -- close the v1 TEXT seam one statement kind per session, biggest first: `local` (337 corpus statements; `p-local` from v1's 1,068-line `_process_local_declaration`), `use`/`no`/`require` (411; the phase model already has the form), `BEGIN` (147), signatured subs with defaults/slurpy placeholders (89; generalise `sig-classic`), loop-modifier statements (47; generalise #3375's desugar), the tail (22); then DELETE `Pl::CLForm::raw`, `fallback_parser`, the 33 `_process_*`, the 53 text heads.  Each kind is an EMISSION change (generation bump, sweep, corpus-diff explained per file).  Bar: seam statements 1,058 -> 0 on the review's 120-file corpus (`PCL_V2_SEAM_CENSUS=1`); `is_raw` calls 160k -> 0 per module; Pl/Parser.pm 13,562 lines -> its pre-pass/facts half only.  4-6 sessions, interleaved with the 1c ports (each kind deletes v1 code the ports would otherwise carry).
  C3 -- facts on BINDING IDS = 1c's consumer side: VarAnnotator and the facts keyed by the binder's binding id; `_let_bound_vars` (51 uses, 12 save/restore sites) -> the binder's scope query; one context encoding.  Bar: `_let_bound_vars` 51 -> 0; corpus-diff IDENTICAL.
  The parser slot's ORDER from here: 1a (the expect-state REPAIR pass consuming the tables + the registry) -> C1 -> the 1c ports (requalifier first: docs/binder-dual-run-s525.md Â§6, fixes #3800 #3801 #3804 by construction) interleaved with C2 kinds -> 1b.  Fillers for any slot: C4 the void-position bind as a Kind-A gate (`p-void-ctx` 8,636 -> after; measure first; bench bar), C5 #75's constructor macros with the next generation bump, C6 name the `use integer` arithmetic heads (host leaks 31 -> 17), C7 rule-10 splits (`gen_funcall_form` 853 lines by builtin family).  R4's code half (`p-setf` to one arm) follows from C1 + C2 (the review's Â§2b store census is its measure: `p-setf` 483 -> toward 0).

=== s527 (Fable, 2026-10-24 evening): 1a RE-POINTED ===
The USER asked whether fixing PPI itself is simpler than the repair engine; measured YES (docs/ppi-fix-at-source-s527.md): 12 token sections fixed in 54 lines of PPI against 1,313 lines of PCL repairs.  RULED: PCL uses its own patched PPI (a branch on upstream master, vendored; brief s527/s527a-prompt.md; umbrella #3697).  Step 1a "ONE expect-state repair pass" is therefore PPI's fixed tokenizer for the token rows; the s526a engine brief is superseded for them; the checker (c1) stays as the detector; the structure rows wait for the same route through PPI's Lexer.  1b (the keyword-class table) and 1c (the binder ports) are unchanged.

Step (1) 1a for the TOKEN rows is now PPI's own fixed tokenizer (PCL's pcl branch, vendored as vendor/PPI; #3697, docs/ppi-fix-at-source-s527.md Â§8): 12 token rows fixed at the source, 2 PCL repairs deleted so far (Â§16 ^^, Â§23 non-ASCII $ names); the expect-state checker (Pl/PPIExpect.pm) remains as the detector.  The parser program resumes after s527b/c/d (review doc Â§8 plan).

=== s527b ===
The token-row half of step 1 continues on PCL's own PPI: s527b deleted 12 more PCL repair passes / subs (the term-end family §4 §12 §25 §28 §38 + §1 §7 §22/§35 §24 §26 §30 §32) and narrowed two (§15/§34, §21) to what only PCL's prototype table knows; the expect-state checker is the instrument (raw 1,280 / pcl 1,230 after, the composition in #3697's s527b section; #3946 = its false rows on Attribute tokens).  Repairs LEFT for the parser program: §27 _brace_glob_slot_symbol (the lowering needs the braced spelling), §8 _strip_decl_decorations (semantics, not a repair), §9 _fold_braced_punct_magic + braced_punct_magic_name, §14 _repair_readline_cascade / _repair_glob_pattern_cascade / PExpr::_fix_ppi_glob_after_block (now also reading group P's Symbol `*>`), §20 _pcl_feature_include_cb -- §9 §14 §20 are s527d's.
